game: DET @ BAL / 2025-09-22 20:15 ET / BAL -4.5 / total 53.5 / outdoors, weather forecast not saved

script.base: Market has Baltimore leading a high-scoring game, not a blowout: implied BAL 29.0, DET 24.5 off a 53.5 total and a 4.5 home number. Base flow is competitive into the fourth quarter, both QBs throwing, Henry (29 carries, 192 yards in two games) grinding late if BAL is in front, and Gibbs/Montgomery still getting a real rush share because Detroit is not forced to abandon the run at -4.5. Pace should be up with the total, so volume matters more than a pure clock-kill.
script.flip1: Baltimore jumps ahead by two scores early behind Henry (169-yard game already on the log) and Jackson's 8/83 rushing. Detroit then tilts pass: Gibbs/Montgomery rush yards die, and St. Brown (17 targets), LaPorta (13), and Jameson Williams (160 air yards) become the DET offense. BAL starters' late pass volume is only mildly at risk — 4.5 is not a true blowout flag.
script.flip2: Shootout stays tied or Detroit hangs around, so both teams stay in the 20s and Henry never gets a 20-carry closeout. Flowers (already 20 targets / 218 yards / 225 air) and the DET pass game all clear together. The other flip is an outdoor slog if wind/rain shows up — forecast was not saved, so that path is unpriced.

injury_fallout: Source: nflverse pre-game injury report, morning of 2025-09-22; final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) not in the pack. BAL OUT: DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) weakens the interior DET will run at — Gibbs (21 car/113, 5.4 YPC) and Montgomery (22/82, 3.7 YPC) are the gainers, and their stand-in rush numbers have no price to show a move. LB Kyle Van Noy (hamstring) out is an edge/pass-rush loss, so Goff gets cleaner pockets; TE/RB checkdowns (LaPorta, Gibbs 13 targets, -3 air) benefit if BAL has to replace him in sub. FB Patrick Ricard (calf) out costs Henry a lead blocker in short yardage — small efficiency hit, not a role change. TE Isaiah Likely (foot) out does not create a new target bump: weeks 1-2 target log already has 0 Likely targets (Flowers 20, Bateman 8, Hill 5, Andrews 4, Hopkins 4). Andrews has no prop here, so the sleeper cannot be bet. DET OUT: DE Marcus Davenport (chest) — Jackson/Flowers gain time; DET edge run defense is thinner, which hurts a Henry under. DET QUESTIONABLE, not treated as out: T Taylor Decker (shoulder) — if he sits, DET pressure up, rush efficiency down, deep yards (Williams 160 air, St. Brown 141 air) down, quick throws to Gibbs/LaPorta up. CB D.J. Reed (knee) and S Kerby Joseph (knee) Q — if both sit, Flowers/Hopkins shot plays face depth; if they play, that boost is gone. LB Jack Campbell (ankle) Q — if he sits, Henry and BAL RB/TE checks face a backup. Re-check inactives before any of these legs is real.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack (step 4 limited). Proxies only: BAL blitzes 25%, DET blitzes 35%. DET EPA/db is 1.18 vs blitz and only 0.21 vs no blitz, so Detroit's offense has been much better when extra rushers come — and Baltimore usually does not bring them. BAL EPA/db is 0.31 vs blitz and 0.45 vs none, so Detroit's 35% blitz has not shut Jackson down in this two-game sample.
matchup.pressure: BAL pressure is the lower-blitz side (25%). Van Noy out should drop that further and help DET time-to-throw. DET brings heat more often (35%) but is without Davenport, so the blitz rate may not equal pressure rate tonight. Pressure that does get home would cut Williams/Hopkins deep yards and lift Gibbs and LaPorta catches — receptions are not a legal market here, so that shows up only inside rush+rec and rec yards.
matchup.bleeds: BAL defense: rush YPC allowed 4.56 but only 3 runs of 10+ in two games (efficiency leak, not a home-run defense). Pass YPA left 7.39 (38 att), middle 9.83 (18), right 4.16 (37) — they bleed the middle and hold the right. 20+ passes: 10/96, a lot of explosives. DET defense: rush YPC 4.18 but 7 runs of 10+ (chunk runs, better per-carry). Pass YPA left 6.44 (16), middle 11.94 (16), right 5.57 (23) — middle is the worst zone on the slate. 20+ passes: 7/59.
matchup.overlap: Cleanest mapped overlap is positional, not charted. Flowers is BAL's primary (20 of 45 team targets, 218 yards, 225 air) into DET's middle at 11.94 YPA, with Davenport already out and Reed/Joseph questionable. On the other side LaPorta (13 tgt, 105 yards, 63 air) is the TE who lives in the middle where BAL allows 9.83 YPA; St. Brown is the actual target leader (17/160/141 air) but his alignment is not in the pack, so he is not the bet. Williams (9 tgt, 131 yards, 160 air) overlaps BAL's 10 explosive passes, but the 23-yard game and Decker's shoulder make it the volatile version of the same idea.

pre_mortem: It's Monday night and both leans lost. Flowers finished near 75 again because Reed and Joseph played, Detroit's middle number was two games of noise, and Baltimore got the lead and fed Henry while the 109.5 stand-in was just his hot average with no actual stale price underneath it. Gibbs finished near 50 rush+rec because Detroit trailed early, Decker was inactive, Montgomery took the between-the-tackles work (he already has 22 carries to Gibbs's 21), and the receiving half stayed at 10 yards — Madubuike being out added a few YPC that never showed up in a 8-carry night. The counter-case is as live as the read, which is why both are leans and the card is flagged.
slip_story: One high-total competitive script, not a mix of under and overs. BAL's 29 implied points flow through Flowers into Detroit's middle, and DET stays in the game with Gibbs all-purpose work against a front missing Madubuike. Those two win together if the 53.5 game shows up and neither team is blown out by halftime. They do not belong with a game under, a Henry rush over, or a Decker-out deep shot (Williams). No TD legs, one market per player, two legs only. Main slip is a candidate stack, not a bet.
